sourcing_note: Sourced from FierceBiotech's annual 'top clinical trial flops' retrospectives (2022 and 2023 editions, accessed via live site and Wayback Machine where the live site did not render), cross-checked against SEC EDGAR and issuer/newswire primary sources. Chosen specifically for likely liquidity (each sponsor was a multi-hundred-million-to-multi-billion dollar Nasdaq-listed biotech at the time), unlike the first newly-sourced batch's single memory-recalled small-cap. Deduplicated against the full existing ticker/candidate_id set. No candidate here was selected or excluded based on its post-event stock outcome.

events.indication: previously untreated unresectable or metastatic melanoma
events.corroborating_sec_accepted: 2022-03-14 07:13:59 ET (Form 8-K, CIK 0000906709, accession 0001213900-22-011983; 15 minutes after the wire release)
events.notes: Failed all three primary endpoints (ORR, PFS, OS) of the 783-patient PIVOT IO-001 trial. Triggered Bristol Myers Squibb to walk away from a collaboration worth up to $3.6B in milestones (on top of a $1.85B 2018 upfront), followed by sweeping Nektar layoffs. One of the most consequential biotech Phase 3 failures of 2022 per FierceBiotech's retrospective.

events.indication: second/third-line advanced non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer

Session classification (after-hours, cutoff = the same day's already-completed session) is not sensitive to the exact minute.
events.notes: SAPPHIRE final analysis did not meet its primary endpoint of overall survival vs. docetaxel. Mirati discontinued the program; the company itself was acquired by Bristol Myers Squibb for $5.8B five months later (October 2023) on the strength of its separate KRAS franchise, unrelated to this failure.

events.timestamp_ambiguity: No mirror displays an explicit release clock time; the SEC 8-K acceptance (06:45:38 ET, pre-market) is used as the primary-source proxy.
events.notes: GLEAM and GLIMMER (identically designed Phase 3 studies, ~460 and 457 patients) both missed their primary non-inferiority endpoint vs. aflibercept, with an unexpected increase in cataracts contributing to the failure. This press release also reported positive results from a third, separate Phase 3 study (BEACON, retinal vein occlusion) - only the GLEAM/GLIMMER DME failure is being registered here as the negative event; BEACON is not being added as a separate candidate in this batch.
